ambient_events: A machine reaches its spin cycle and the whole floor hums through your boots.
The dryer at the end thumps twice, considers stopping, and carries on.
Warm air breathes out from under the row of machines, smelling of soap and hot metal.
Someone's forgotten sock sits on top of the folding table, waiting with infinite patience.
The kettle in the corner clicks off. Nobody made the tea.
Rain finds the window and runs down it in long warm streaks. In here it doesn't matter.
description: Eight machines along the left wall, four dryers facing them, and between the two rows a strip of floor kept warm all night by the pair of them. The window is the whole front of the building, real glass cleaned often enough to prove someone cares, and the light coming off it spills a long pale rectangle onto Ironside Street outside, which is why people find this place before they know what it is. There's a folding table worn smooth at the edges, a bench along the back with a cushion somebody re-covered by hand, and a kettle on a shelf beside a jar of teabags with TAKE ONE, LEAVE ONE inked on the lid. A hand-lettered card is taped to the middle machine: Broke? Wash anyway. Pay when you can. Nobody has ever been chased out of here for sleeping in the warm. Out east to the street.
name: The Wash
